newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end down, SBI net meets expectation.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end down, SBI net meets expectation.

text.p: Bombay shares finished in negative territory on Thursday after moving in a narrow trading range, as more company results came in, dealers said.
The benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) 30-share index fell 15.77 points, or 0.55 percent, to close at a provisional 2,867.80 --off the day's high of 2,910.0.

Market-favourite State Bank of India (SBI), the country's largest commercial bank, announced a 179 percent rise in its six month net profit ending September 30, 1996 to 6.41 billion rupees against 2.30 billion in the year-ago period.
The firm's results came just after close of market hours.
Shares of SBI dropped 2.75 rupees to end at 216.25, after rallying to 222.0 rupees at the BSE in volumes of over 4.7 million shares.
"SBI results were as per market expectations. The market was expecting anything around 6.5-7.5 billion rupees," said chief dealer Ketan Jhaveri at local brokerage Kotak Securities.
Traders said the stock was quoted higher at 220.0/221.50 rupees in kerb deals late on Thursday.
Power firm BSES said its first half 1996/97 (April-March) net profit rose 11.0 percent to 941.9 million rupees compared to 850.2 million rupees in the previous year.
The stock which announced results during trading hours ended 3.50 rupees down at 195.50, off 202.50 rupees.

Traders said low volumes and little action by foreign funds kept share prices range-bound. The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index fell 4.0 points, or 0.48 percent, to a provisional close of 825.0.

ACC lost 7.50 rupees to 1,010 rupees, Reliance 0.50 to 180.75, Bajaj Auto 9.25 to 825.0, Tata Power 1.75 to 107.25 and Gujarat Ambuja 14.50 to 239.75. TISCO rose 0.25 rupees to 153.75, BHEL 2.75 to 190.25 and ITC 3.0 to 277.0.
